notes: Learning Primitives are modular educational units.
No personalized advice or final customer conversation is manufactured in this asset.

content.canonical_meaning: A policy condition where the policyholder pays a fixed percentage of every admissible claim amount.
content.text: Copay means you agree to pay a fixed percentage of every approved insurance claim.

primitives.learning_objective: Customer should be able to define Copay.

content.text: Insurance companies first determine how much of your hospital bill is payable under your policy. Only after that is Copay calculated.

primitives.learning_objective: Customer understands that Copay is calculated after claim review.

steps: Customer Pays Non-payable Items plus Copay

primitives.learning_objective: Customer understands who pays what during a Copay claim.

content.explanation: 20% is applied on ₹90,000, not on ₹1,00,000. The ₹10,000 non-payable amount is added separately.

primitives.learning_objective: Customer can calculate Copay correctly using approved claim amount.

content.correction: Copay is calculated on the insurer-approved amount. Expenses not payable under the policy are paid separately.
content.misconception: Copay means I pay only 20% of the total hospital bill.

source_misinterpretations.actual_meaning: Copay applies on the admissible claim amount approved by the insurer.
source_misinterpretations.misinterpretation: Copay applies on the total hospital bill.

source_misinterpretations.actual_meaning: Customer may also pay non-payable expenses separately.
source_misinterpretations.misinterpretation: Copay is the only amount customer pays.

primitives.learning_objective: Customer avoids the common incorrect expectation that Copay is the only amount payable.

content.business_purpose: Share claim cost between insurer and customer, often in exchange for lower premium.
content.text: Policies with Copay usually cost less because the customer shares a portion of every claim.

content.boundary: This is not a recommendation. Final suitability depends on customer context.
may_be_suitable_when: Customer is comfortable sharing claim costs.
may_not_be_suitable_when: Customer may not be comfortable paying during hospitalization.

primitives.learning_objective: Customer understands when a Copay policy may or may not be suitable.
Customer can connect Copay with nearby insurance concepts.

content.answer: No. You may also pay expenses that are not covered by the policy.
content.question: Will I always pay only the Copay percentage?

primitives.learning_objective: Customer can answer whether they will always pay only the Copay percentage.

content.text: Always explain Copay using an actual claim example. Customers rarely misunderstand the definition; they misunderstand the calculation.

primitives.learning_objective: Advisor understands how to explain Copay clearly.

policy_examples.result: Customer pays ₹10,000 non-payable amount plus ₹18,000 copay; insurer pays ₹72,000.
policy_examples.scenario: Hospital bill is ₹1,00,000, admissible claim is ₹90,000, and copay is 20%.

primitives.learning_objective: Advisor can trace the learning primitive back to the source meaning example.
